analysis.title: The AI Put Is Now The Treasury Market's Last Line Of Defense, BofA Warns
key_insights: Last Tuesday's 5Y Treasury auction priced at 5.033%, the first 5-handle since 2007, with the second-biggest tail on record and the lowest bid-to-cover since 2018. Bonds had their worst day since Liberation Day.
Yields hit multi-decade highs across the curve. The 10Y briefly rose above 5.3% on Friday, the highest since 2004, and the 30Y yields well above 5.6%. The MOVE index rose above 100.
Stocks have not reacted. The VIX is still comparatively calm and the Nasdaq rose more than 3% last week on Meta's Muse agentic assistant.

BofA equity derivatives says macro faces 'a high bar to derail the AI trade.' With a relatively fixed supply of attention, macro risk struggles to compete with AI growth narratives. AI FOMO drives dip-buying, which BofA calls the 'AI put.'

BofA historical comparison: in the 1990s internet boom, long-end rates rose 200bps and the Fed hiked 100bps while the equity bubble kept building. BofA equity strategists 'don't see 5% yields as a necessary death knell for stocks.'
BofA sees rates vol as 'relatively contained' and far from 2022 extremes. Changing that would take much higher yields and/or rates vol, which would likely require a lack of policymaker intervention.

The main risk BofA names is an AI-narrative slip-up that reprices growth lower and worsens macro stress. Without the AI put, all other risks could be materially amplified. BofA sees that risk as 'further out on the horizon' because fundamentals are strong and valuations are de-rating rather than stretching.

BofA now publishes its Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI) weekly. Tech reads about 0.72 and healthcare about 0.76, against a danger line of 0.8. Semis had the biggest one-week BRI jump of any popular theme. US Cybersecurity (0.91) and US Healthcare Momentum (0.85) are the only themes in bubble territory.

Breadth does not look like 1999. Only 18 S&P 500 stocks have a BRI above 0.8, against 50 to 100 at dotcom peaks. They are 3.2% of index weight, against 20% to 40% then. The top names are MRNA, CRWD, HPE and RVTY.

BofA's Global Financial Stress Indicator rose from -0.10 to -0.05 last week. EUR and USD rates implied vol had the two largest stress increases of any subcomponent, in the 97th and 95th percentiles of history. Rates vol is the most stressed cross-asset vol measure since March, replacing commodity vol.

USDJPY skew is the most stressed FX gauge and the only one in bearish territory. Credit stress is also rising: EUR 3Y/5Y credit curves, USD IG CDS and EUR HY CDS all posted stress gains in the top decile of their history.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA says AI FOMO drives dip-buying and macro faces a high bar to derail the AI trade. Fundamentals are strong, valuations are de-rating rather than stretching, and the 1990s saw long-end rates rise 200bps while the equity bubble continued.
tension_points.bear_case: A slip-up in the AI narrative would reprice growth lower and amplify macro stress, since the AI put is mitigating fiscal and rates risk. Rates vol, credit and FX skew stress are already rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A disappointment in the AI narrative, or much higher yields and/or rates vol without policymaker intervention.
